question.questionText: I ______ all day, so I wasn't tired and went to the disco at night.
question.explanationHtml:

The blank needs a verb tense that shows an action that did not happen over a period of time before another past event. The sentence describes that the person was not tired and went to the disco at night because they had not been working all day. The correct tense to use is the past perfect continuous negative ('had not been working'), which emphasizes the duration of not working before going to the disco.

  • had worked (verb phrase): Past perfect simple: shows a completed action before another past event, but does not emphasize duration.
  • had not worked (verb phrase): Past perfect simple negative: shows a completed action that did not happen before another past event, but does not emphasize duration.
  • had not been worked (verb phrase): Incorrect passive form; 'work' is not usually used in the passive in this context.
Related structure or vocabulary: Past perfect continuous tense (had been + V-ing) is used to show an action that was happening over a period of time before another action in the past, especially to emphasize duration.
